problem: Modular zero-shot ObjectNav methods with foundation models rely on observation-bounded scene representations. With poor viewpoints or weak semantic cues, detection produces false positives/negatives and locally greedy frontier scoring gives small score margins, causing redundant exploration and backtracking.
motivation: Targets and related objects/regions share inherent spatial regularities (orientation, distance, topology) that persist even when the target is unseen. Encoding these as experience-based priors together with observations should help early exploration, when visual information is scarce, and help verify uncertain detections.
key_idea: Build a target-centered Dynamic Spatial Relationship Graph (LLM commonsense priors refined online by VLM-inferred observed relations) and use it both to verify or correct detections by relation matching and to plan frontier selection via relational path cues.
insight: Combining experience priors with observations gives useful guidance early in exploration. The module ablation shows the full model reaching 58.3 SR vs 52.5 for the base, with RAMM giving the largest single gain (+3.8 SR, 54.5 to 58.3). The relation ablation shows topology matters most (w/o topo 52.7 SR), while prompt template rewording changes SR only slightly (55.3-56.5), except a bare-target prompt (51.3). This suggests the gains are structural rather than prompt-engineering artifacts.
method: DSRG initialization: DeepSeek-R1 is prompted offline to generate topological, directional and distance relations around the target category, stored as a JSON graph with object and region nodes.

Graph refinement / node verification: an instance-level existence confidence combines detection confidence, observation quality, expected visibility and temporal continuity (beta=0.6, rho=0.8, L=5, lambda=0.8). Nodes are inserted at confidence > 0.8; Qwen2.5-VL-7B infers object-target and room-level relations, fused by a confidence-weighted update.

RAMM: matches detections against DSRG relations and the current region to classify them as TP, FP or FN. The VLM then verifies FPs using crop, context and relational constraints, and re-detects FNs from a descriptive prompt to output bounding boxes.
DRPM guidance generation: the VLM localizes the agent in the DSRG, infers relational paths to the target, and produces region and object cues as prompts (e.g. 'Seems like a Region-cues is ahead').

Frontier selection: frontiers come from a 2D obstacle map (Yamauchi). The frontier whose view has highest VLM (BLIP-2-style, VLFM-like) cosine similarity to the relational prompt is chosen. VLFM's local point-nav planner executes it.
Perception stack: YOLOv7 for COCO classes, Grounding DINO for open vocabulary, and SAM for 3D object information from RGB-D.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen) for relation inference/verification; DeepSeek-R1 for offline graph priors; BLIP-2-style VLM similarity as in VLFM; YOLOv7 + Grounding DINO + SAM
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 480x640 (depth 0.5-5 m, HFOV 79°) with odometry
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° / STOP, with frontier waypoints via VLFM point-nav planner

results: On HM3D, SR-Nav gets 58.3 SR / 33.0 SPL, beating WMNav-Gemini (58.1/31.2) and Uni-Nav (54.5/25.1). On MP3D it gets 37.7 SR / 17.1 SPL, below Uni-Nav (41.0 SR) and WMNav-Gemini (45.4 SR), but SPL is competitive. It also runs at 1.5 min/episode vs 13 for SG-Nav.
limitations: MP3D SR (37.7) trails Uni-Nav and WMNav-Gemini, so the gain does not generalize across benchmarks.
Relies on many external models (LLM, VLM, detectors, SAM) and offline LLM priors, and the real-world evaluation is only qualitative (one potted-plant example).
Table 1 lists 'WMNav-Gemini' and 'Uni-Nav' as baselines that the text claims are beaten on HM3D by only a narrow margin; no variance or multiple seeds are reported.
